newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty seen capped, yields up next week.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty seen capped, yields up next week.

text.p: The Polish zloty is likely to remain capped under strong resistance at three percent from the parity rate next week after battling repeated National Bank of Poland (NBP) interventions this week, dealers said on Friday.

Dealers also said that recent price cuts in Polish treasuries would be continued at next Monday's primary T-bill auction, but they still expected demand to fall well short of the finance ministry's one billion zloty offer.

"The zloty will hold at three percent -- the level the central bank showed it wants to see the currency -- with a downward drift possible if the NBP steps in again," said Bogdan Stepkowski, senior forex dealer at ING bank in Warsaw.

Some said the NBP's currency-buying cooled the market's pro-zloty sentiment enough that next week players could refrain from speculative currency sales, which had driven the zloty up in recent weeks along with foreign entry into Polish bonds.
"The zloty should trade between 2.7 and 3.0 percent from parity next week," said Jaroslaw Dryjski from Bank Slaski SA.

Dealers said that foreign investors, who bought most of the 200 million zlotys worth of 12-percent fixed bonds sold on Thursday, were more likely to buy zlotys for their bonds at the central bank's post-trade fixing than during trade.
"Many foreigners may buy zlotys at the fixing because it is safer, so trade may not be effected at all," one dealer said.
The value date for the fixed bonds, whose maximum yield amounted to 19.46 percent for just over four years, is March 5.
The zloty closed the week at 2.96 percent from the trading band centre, down from this week's high above 3.6 percent and last Friday's close at 3.17 percent.
It was at 3.0470 to the dollar, down from last Friday's 3.0310 and at 1.8090 to the mark, also down from 1.7985.
Dealers expected yields on all maturities to rise above 20 percent at Monday's T-bill tender after the finance ministry said it would increase yields to boost demand for treasuries.
"Everything should be above 20 percent with investor demand expected at up to 500 million zlotys," said Piotr Korcz, T-bill dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers said foreigners would likely refrain from larger T-bill purchases until yields hit resistance in several weeks time.
They expected the average yield of the benchmark 52-week paper to rise above 20.20 percent from 20.07, with maximum yields hitting as high as 20.55 percent against this week's 20.40.

Dealers said money market one-day rates would likely hover around 22.5 percent next week as banks had surpluses on their required reserve accounts going into the last week of the February reserve, which ends on Thursday.

"One-day cash should remain at present levels unless the NBP drains the market heavily as banks seem to have surpluses, but are reluctant to place cash at cheap rates," said Aleksandra Watroba, deposit dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
The central bank drained more than one billion zlotys in reverse repos this week after not staging any reverse repo operations for the first two weeks of February.
Overnight rates closed the week at 22.30 percent and tomorrow/next rates at 22.35 percent.
